plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Organization currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW).

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: Organization timezone (e.g., Asia/Seoul, America/New_York).

plainFields.name: fiscal_start_month
plainFields.description: Fiscal year start month (1-12).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Organization status (active, archived, deleted).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Record deletion timestamp for soft delete.

models.name: hrm_tracker_pending_invitations
models.description: Pending invitations for employee onboarding before user signup. Each invitation is associated with an organization and an email address.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Target organization that sent the invitation.

foreignFields.name: invited_by_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who sent the invitation.

foreignFields.name: invited_by_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Session context when the invitation was sent.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address of the invited person. Must be unique within the organization.

plainFields.name: message
plainFields.description: Optional message included in the invitation email.

plainFields.name: role_name
plainFields.description: Role name to assign to the invited employee (e.g., 'Manager', 'Employee').

plainFields.name: department_name
plainFields.description: Department name to assign to the invited employee (optional).

plainFields.name: invited_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was sent.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was resolved (user signed up and became employee).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Invitation status: 'pending', 'accepted', 'expired', or 'cancelled'. Default is 'pending'.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique token for invitation link. Used for verification when user signs up.

models.name: hrm_tracker_organization_settings
models.description: Organization configuration settings including fiscal start month, currency, timezone, and other organizational preferences.

plainFields.name: fiscal_start_month
plainFields.description: Fiscal year start month (1-12). Required for financial reporting and budgeting.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Organization's currency code (ISO 4217). Examples: USD, EUR, KRW.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: Organization's timezone (IANA timezone name). Examples: Asia/Seoul, America/New_York.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name of the organization for this settings context.

plainFields.name: logo_url
plainFields.description: URL to the organization's logo image.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

models.name: hrm_tracker_employees
models.description: Employee records linked to users within an organization. Each employee belongs to exactly one organization and can be assigned a role for permission management.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the employee record.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization's id. Employee belongs to exactly one organization.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Member's id. Employee record links to the user account.

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description: Role's id. Current assigned role for this employee in the organization.

foreignFields.name: department_id
foreignFields.description: Department's id. Optional department归属. Set to NULL when department is deleted.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Employee status. Values: 'active', 'deactivated'. Deactivated employees cannot log time or submit timesheets.

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description: Employment type classification. Values: 'full-time', 'part-time', 'contractor', 'intern'.

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description: Employee's position or title within the organization.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp. Automatically set when employee record is created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp. Automatically updated on every change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. NULL for active employees, set when employee is deactivated.

models.name: hrm_tracker_roles
models.description:
Roles defined per organization assigned to employees. Each role belongs to exactly one organization and can be assigned to multiple employees. Roles can be built-in (Owner, Manager, Employee) or custom, with custom roles supporting detailed permission sets through the hrm_tracker_role_permissions junction table.

Organization-scoped: Roles are isolated to their parent organization and cannot be shared across organizations.

Deletion constraint: Custom roles (is_custom = true) can only be deleted if no employees are currently assigned to them.

foreignFields.name: hrm_tracker_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization that owns this role. {@link hrm_tracker_organizations.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique role name within the organization (e.g., Owner, Manager, Employee, or custom name). Required for both built-in and custom roles.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description explaining the role's purpose and responsibilities.

plainFields.name: is_custom
plainFields.description: Whether this is a custom role created by the organization (true) or a built-in role (false). Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be deleted.

plainFields.name: is_default
plainFields.description: Whether this role is automatically assigned to newly invited employees. Organizations can set one default role.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this role was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this role was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for archival purposes. Roles are never hard-deleted; deleted_at indicates retirement.

models.name: hrm_tracker_permissions
models.description:
Assigns permissions to roles within the organization.

This table defines which permissions are granted to each role. Each role can have multiple permissions, and each permission can be assigned to multiple roles (many-to-many relationship).

**Permission Values:**

- org:manage: Full organization management access
- employee:manage: Manage employees (invite, deactivate, view all)
- employee:view: View employee information
- project:manage: Manage projects, tasks, and project members
- project:view: View project information
- time:manage: Manage own timelogs and timers
- time:approve: Approve/reject timesheets
- time:view_all: View all timelogs across the organization
- report:view: Access organization reports

**Relationships:**

- Belongs to exactly one role (hrm_tracker_roles)
- One role can have many permissions

**Data Integrity:**

- Composite unique constraint on role_id and permission_name
- Foreign key to hrm_tracker_roles with CASCADE delete
- Permission names are validated at application level

**Usage:**

- Assigned to roles during role creation/editing
- Checked during authorization to grant/deny access
- Inherited by all employees with that role

**Example:**

- Manager role might have: project:manage, time:approve, report:view
- Employee role might have: project:view, time:manage, time:view_all

### `hrm_tracker_guests`

Guest identification records with device-based fingerprinting.

Guests are unauthenticated users who can access the system before signing
up. They are identified by device fingerprint and have no organization
context or role. When guests sign up and join an organization, they
become members.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `device_fingerprint`: Unique device identifier for guest identification.
- `email`: Email address for authentication (set during signup).
- `password_hash`: Encrypted password for authentication.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the guest record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the guest record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was deleted (soft delete).

### `hrm_tracker_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access without authentication.

This table records guest session events with connection metadata. Guest
sessions are used for anonymous access patterns and do not require
email/password authentication.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `guest_id`: Guest user's [hrm_tracker_guests.id](#hrm_tracker_guests).
- `ip`: Client IP address at session start.

### `hrm_tracker_members`

Member accounts with email/password authentication, profile information,
and status. Members can belong to multiple organizations through employee
records. Supports soft deletion for audit trail preservation. Each member
has one global profile shared across all organizations they belong to.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the member account.
- `email`: Unique email address for authentication and communication.
- `password_hash`: BCrypt hashed password for secure authentication.
- `display_name`: Global display name visible across all organizations.
- `avatar_url`: URL to member's avatar image. Global profile shared across organizations.
- `phone`: Contact phone number for the member.
- `status`
  > Account status: 'active' (can use system), 'deactivated' (disabled by
  > admin/system).
- `email_verified`: Whether the email address has been verified by the member.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the member account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. NULL for active accounts.

### `hrm_tracker_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens with access and refresh capabilities for member
authentication. Stores active sessions with token information and
connection metadata for security auditing.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`: Member who owns this session. [hrm_tracker_members.id](#hrm_tracker_members).
- `access_token`: Access token for API authentication.
- `refresh_token`: Refresh token for session renewal.
- `ip`: IP address of the client when session was created.
- `user_agent`: User agent string from client browser/device.
- `created_at`: When this session was created.
- `expires_at`: When this session will expire.

### `hrm_tracker_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens with expiration for member account recovery.
Records are created when members request password reset, used to verify
identity, and automatically expire after the specified time.

Properties as follows:

- `hrm_tracker_member_id`
  > The member account requesting password reset. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_members.id}.
- `token`: Unique password reset token.
- `expires_at`: When this password reset token expires.
- `ip`: IP address where the password reset request was made.
- `used_at`: When this password reset token was used.
- `created_at`: When this password reset token was created.
- `updated_at`: When this password reset token was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: When this password reset token was soft-deleted.

### `hrm_tracker_member_email_verifications`

Email verification tokens for confirming member email addresses during
registration.

This table stores temporary verification tokens that are sent to users
during registration
to verify their email address ownership. The tokens expire after a
certain period and
must be verified before the member account becomes fully active.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.

- `verified_at`: Timestamp when email was successfully verified. NULL until verified.

### `hrm_tracker_employees`

Employee records linked to users within an organization. Each employee
belongs to exactly one organization and can be assigned a role for
permission management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the employee record.
- `organization_id`: Organization's id. Employee belongs to exactly one organization.
- `user_id`: Member's id. Employee record links to the user account.
- `role_id`: Role's id. Current assigned role for this employee in the organization.
- `department_id`
  > Department's id. Optional department归属. Set to NULL when department is
  > deleted.
- `status`
  > Employee status. Values: 'active', 'deactivated'. Deactivated employees
  > cannot log time or submit timesheets.
- `employment_type`
  > Employment type classification. Values: 'full-time', 'part-time',
  > 'contractor', 'intern'.
- `position`: Employee's position or title within the organization.
- `created_at`
  > Record creation timestamp. Automatically set when employee record is
  > created.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp. Automatically updated on every change.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. NULL for active employees, set when employee is
  > deactivated.

### `hrm_tracker_roles`

Roles defined per organization assigned to employees. Each role belongs
to exactly one organization and can be assigned to multiple employees.
Roles can be built-in (Owner, Manager, Employee) or custom, with custom
roles supporting detailed permission sets through the
hrm_tracker_role_permissions junction table.

Organization-scoped: Roles are isolated to their parent organization and
cannot be shared across organizations.

Deletion constraint: Custom roles (is_custom = true) can only be deleted
if no employees are currently assigned to them.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `hrm_tracker_organization_id`: Organization that owns this role. [hrm_tracker_organizations.id](#hrm_tracker_organizations).
- `name`
  > Unique role name within the organization (e.g., Owner, Manager, Employee,
  > or custom name). Required for both built-in and custom roles.
- `description`: Optional description explaining the role's purpose and responsibilities.
- `is_custom`
  > Whether this is a custom role created by the organization (true) or a
  > built-in role (false). Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot
  > be deleted.
- `is_default`
  > Whether this role is automatically assigned to newly invited employees.
  > Organizations can set one default role.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this role was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this role was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp for archival purposes. Roles are never
  > hard-deleted; deleted_at indicates retirement.

### `hrm_tracker_permissions`

Assigns permissions to roles within the organization.

This table defines which permissions are granted to each role. Each role
can have multiple permissions, and each permission can be assigned to
multiple roles (many-to-many relationship).

**Permission Values:**

- org:manage: Full organization management access
- employee:manage: Manage employees (invite, deactivate, view all)
- employee:view: View employee information
- project:manage: Manage projects, tasks, and project members
- project:view: View project information
- time:manage: Manage own timelogs and timers
- time:approve: Approve/reject timesheets
- time:view_all: View all timelogs across the organization
- report:view: Access organization reports

**Relationships:**

- Belongs to exactly one role (hrm_tracker_roles)
- One role can have many permissions

**Data Integrity:**

- Composite unique constraint on role_id and permission_name
- Foreign key to hrm_tracker_roles with CASCADE delete
- Permission names are validated at application level

**Usage:**

- Assigned to roles during role creation/editing
- Checked during authorization to grant/deny access
- Inherited by all employees with that role

**Example:**

- Manager role might have: project:manage, time:approve, report:view
- Employee role might have: project:view, time:manage, time:view_all

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the permission assignment record.
- `hrm_tracker_role_id`
  > Belonged role's [hrm_tracker_roles.id](#hrm_tracker_roles). The role to which this
  > permission is assigned.
- `permission`
  > Permission code following org:entity:action format.
  >
  > Allowed values:
  >
  > - org:manage: Full organization management access
  > - employee:manage: Manage employees (invite, deactivate, view all)
  > - employee:view: View employee information
  > - project:manage: Manage projects, tasks, and project members
  > - project:view: View project information
  > - time:manage: Manage own timelogs and timers
  > - time:approve: Approve/reject timesheets
  > - time:view_all: View all timelogs across the organization
  > - report:view: Access organization reports
  >
  > **Format**: `{resource}:{action}`
  >
  > **Examples**:
  > - org:manage
  > - employee:manage
  > - project:manage
  > - time:approve
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this permission was assigned to the role.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this permission assignment was last modified.

### `hrm_tracker_employee_histories`

Historical employee records for audit and point-in-time reporting. This
table captures snapshots of employee data at the time of significant
changes, providing an immutable audit trail of employee record
modifications including role assignments, status changes, and permission
updates. Each record represents the employee state immediately after a
change was made, enabling reconstruction of employee history and
compliance auditing.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `employee_id`
  > Reference to the employee record that was changed. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_employees.id}.
- `changed_by_id`
  > Reference to the member who made the change. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_members.id}.
- `organization_id`
  > Reference to the organization context for data isolation. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_organizations.id}.
- `role_id`
  > Reference to the role assigned at the time of change. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_roles.id}. Nullable when no role assigned.
- `department_id`
  > Reference to the department at the time of change. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_departments.id}. Nullable when department not assigned.
- `action_type`
  > Type of action that triggered this history record (role_assigned,
  > role_changed, status_changed, employee_added, employee_deactivated,
  > etc.).
- `previous_status`: Previous employee status before the change (active, deactivated).
- `current_status`: Current employee status after the change (active, deactivated).
- `previous_position`
  > Previous position/title before the change. Null when position was not set
  > previously.
- `current_position`: Current position/title after the change.
- `previous_employment_type`
  > Previous employment type before the change (full-time, part-time,
  > contractor, intern).
- `current_employment_type`: Current employment type after the change.
- `changed_fields`: Comma-separated list of fields that were changed in this record.
- `change_description`: Human-readable description of the change made.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this historical record was created (when the change
  > occurred).

### `hrm_tracker_employee_role_change_details`

Key-value pairs for JSON details of role changes (e.g., 'old_role',
'new_role', 'changed_by'). Enables atomic storage and querying of
structured audit data while preserving 1NF compliance.

This table stores structured audit details for employee role changes as
separate rows instead of JSON strings, supporting efficient querying of

entry is associated with a parent audit record in
hrm_tracker_employee_role_changes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `change_id`

- `key`
  > Key name of the audit detail (e.g., 'old_role', 'new_role', 'changed_by',
  > 'department_change').
- `value`
  > Value of the audit detail as a string representation (e.g., 'Manager',
  > 'Employee', 'user_id').
- `created_at`: When this audit detail was recorded.
- `updated_at`: When this audit detail was last updated.

### `hrm_tracker_projects`

Projects owned by organizations with name, color, status, budget, and
dates. Projects serve as containers for tasks and project members.
Organization-scoped for multi-tenancy with soft delete support.
Archived/completed projects preserve existing timelogs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. UUID identifier for the project record.
- `hrm_tracker_organization_id`
  > Organization's [hrm_tracker_organizations.id](#hrm_tracker_organizations). Project belongs to
  > this organization for multi-tenancy isolation.
- `name`: Project name (required). Max 255 characters.
- `description`
  > Project description (optional). Can contain detailed project information
  > in markdown format.
- `color`: Color code for UI visualization (required). Hex format (e.g., '#FF5733').
- `status`: Project status (required). Values: 'active', 'archived', 'completed'.
- `budget_hours`
  > Total budgeted hours for the project (optional). Used for budget tracking
  > and variance analysis.
- `start_date`: Project start date (optional). When the project is scheduled to begin.
- `end_date`
  > Project end date (optional). When the project is scheduled to be
  > completed.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null if not deleted.

### `hrm_tracker_project_members`

Assigns employees to projects with role (member or project-lead) and
timestamps.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `hrm_tracker_employee_id`: Referenced employee. [hrm_tracker_employees.id](#hrm_tracker_employees).
- `hrm_tracker_project_id`: Referenced project. [hrm_tracker_projects.id](#hrm_tracker_projects).
- `role`: Role assigned to the employee in this project (member or project-lead).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (nullable for active records).

### `hrm_tracker_tasks`

Tasks belonging to projects with status, priority, assignment, and
optional parent task. Tasks are created by project leads or users with
project:manage permission and can be assigned to project members. Status
changes are tracked in hrm_tracker_task_histories. Subtasks are supported
with one level of nesting through the parent task relationship.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `project_id`: Project this task belongs to. [hrm_tracker_projects.id](#hrm_tracker_projects).
- `assigned_employee_id`
  > Employee assigned to this task (must be project member). {@link
  > hrm_tracker_employees.id}.
- `parent_task_id`
  > Parent task for subtasks (one level nesting only). {@link
  > hrm_tracker_tasks.id}.
- `title`: Task title (required).
- `description`: Task description with details.
- `status`: Task status: open, in-progress, completed, or closed.
- `priority`: Task priority: low, medium, high, or urgent.
- `estimated_hours`: Estimated hours to complete this task.
- `due_date`: Task due date.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (nullable means not deleted).

### `hrm_tracker_task_histories`

Records status change history for tasks with timestamp, actor, and
old/new status. Used for audit trails and tracking task evolution over
time. Each entry captures who made the status change, when it was made,
and what the status changed from and to.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_id`
  > Organization context for multi-tenancy isolation. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_organizations.id}.
- `task_id`: Task whose status changed. [hrm_tracker_tasks.id](#hrm_tracker_tasks).
- `employee_id`
  > Employee who made the status change (actor). {@link
  > hrm_tracker_employees.id}.
- `old_status`: Previous task status before change (open, in-progress, completed, closed).
- `new_status`: New task status after change (open, in-progress, completed, closed).
- `changed_at`: Timestamp when the status change occurred.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (nullable means not deleted).

### `hrm_tracker_timelogs`

Time entries recorded by employees for work performed on projects/tasks.
Each timelog captures the date, duration, and optional task associated
with work performed, organized within an organization context for
multi-tenancy isolation. Timelogs are created by employees for
themselves, linked to projects they're assigned to, and optionally to
specific tasks within those projects. The billable flag indicates whether
the time should be considered for billing purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_id`
  > Organization reference for multi-tenancy isolation. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_organizations.id}.
- `employee_id`: Employee who created this timelog. [hrm_tracker_employees.id](#hrm_tracker_employees).
- `project_id`: Project reference (required). [hrm_tracker_projects.id](#hrm_tracker_projects).
- `task_id`
  > Task reference (optional, must belong to selected project). {@link
  > hrm_tracker_tasks.id}.
- `date`: Date of the timelog entry.
- `duration_in_minutes`: Duration of work in minutes.
- `description`: Optional description of work performed.
- `billable`: Whether this timelog is billable (default true).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for audit trail.

### `hrm_tracker_timesheets`

Timesheet records that aggregate timelogs per employee per week for
payroll and billing. Each timesheet represents a calendar week
(Monday-Sunday) and tracks approval workflow status (draft, submitted,
approved, rejected). Timesheets serve as the formal record for time
tracking, with approved timesheets locking their timelogs to prevent
modification.

Timesheets reference:
- Organization for multi-tenancy isolation
- Employee as the owner who created the timelogs
- Member who reviewed/approved the timesheet

All timesheet operations (create, edit, submit, approve, reject) follow
strict business rules including employee-only creation and timelog
locking on approval.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each timesheet record.
- `hrm_tracker_organization_id`
  > Timesheet's organization for multi-tenancy isolation. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_organizations.id}.
- `hrm_tracker_employee_id`
  > Employee who owns this timesheet and created the timelogs. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_employees.id}.
- `reviewed_by_member_id`
  > Member who reviewed/approved/rejected this timesheet. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_members.id}. Nullable until timesheet is processed.
- `week_start_date`: Start date of the week this timesheet covers (always Monday).
- `week_end_date`: End date of the week this timesheet covers (always Sunday).
- `status`
  > Timesheet status: draft (creating), submitted (submitted for approval),
  > approved (approved by manager), rejected (rejected by manager).
- `total_hours`: Calculated total hours across all timelogs in this timesheet.
- `submitted_at`: Timestamp when employee submitted this timesheet for approval.
- `reviewed_at`: Timestamp when manager reviewed/approved/rejected this timesheet.
- `rejection_reason`
  > Reason provided by manager when rejecting the timesheet. Empty when
  > timesheet is approved or in draft/submitted status.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this timesheet record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this timesheet record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. Nullable until timesheet is deleted.

### `hrm_tracker_timesheet_timelogs`

Junction table linking timesheets and timelogs for flexible aggregation.

This table enables timesheets to include multiple timelogs while supporting
approval workflows where timelogs can be referenced across different states.
All data is organization-scoped for multi-tenancy isolation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `hrm_tracker_timesheet_id`: Reference to the timesheet. @{link hrm_tracker_timesheets.id}.
- `hrm_tracker_timelog_id`: Reference to the timelog. @{link hrm_tracker_timelogs.id}.
- `created_at`: When this timelog was added to the timesheet.

### `hrm_tracker_employee_contracts`

Historical employee contracts with one active at a time per employee.
Each contract records pay rate, pay period, and working hours for an
employee during a specific time period. Only one contract can be active
(is_active = true) per employee at any given time. Past contracts are
immutable and preserved for auditing and reporting purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `hrm_tracker_employee_id`
  > Belonged employee's [hrm_tracker_employees.id](#hrm_tracker_employees). Reference to the
  > employee who owns this contract history.
- `hrm_tracker_organization_id`
  > Belonged organization's [hrm_tracker_organizations.id](#hrm_tracker_organizations).
  > Organization context for multi-tenancy data isolation.
- `start_date`
  > Contract start date (required). The date when this contract becomes
  > effective.
- `end_date`
  > Contract end date (optional). null indicates the contract is still active
  > or has no defined end.
- `pay_rate`: Employee pay rate (required). The monetary amount paid per pay period.
- `pay_period`
  > Pay period type (required). Defines whether pay is calculated hourly,
  > daily, weekly, or monthly.
- `working_hours_per_week`
  > Standard working hours per week (required). Number of hours expected per
  > week for this contract.
- `is_active`
  > Whether this contract is currently active (required). Only one contract
  > can be active per employee at a time.
- `notes`: Additional notes or comments about the contract (optional).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (nullable if not deleted).

### `hrm_tracker_activity_logs`

Activity log records significant system actions for audit trail purposes.
Each entry captures who performed the action (actor), what action was
performed, which entity was affected (target), when it happened, and
additional details. Supports actions like employee management
(invited/deactivated/reactivated), contract changes, project lifecycle
events (created/archived/completed/deleted), task status changes,
timesheet workflow actions (submitted/approved/rejected), and role
assignments. This table serves as the system's audit trail to track all
significant business events for compliance and debugging.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `hrm_tracker_member_id`: Actor (member) who performed this action. [hrm_tracker_members.id](#hrm_tracker_members).
- `hrm_tracker_guest_id`: Actor (guest) who performed this action. [hrm_tracker_guests.id](#hrm_tracker_guests).
- `target_entity_type`
  > Type of entity that was affected by this action (e.g., 'employee',
  > 'contract', 'project', 'task', 'timesheet', 'role', 'pending_invitation',
  > 'organization').
- `target_entity_id`: ID of the entity that was affected by this action.
- `action_type`
  > Type of action that was performed (e.g., 'employee_invited',
  > 'employee_deactivated', 'employee_reactivated', 'contract_created',
  > 'contract_edited', 'project_created', 'project_archived',
  > 'project_completed', 'project_deleted', 'task_status_changed',
  > 'timesheet_submitted', 'timesheet_approved', 'timesheet_rejected',
  > 'role_assigned', 'role_changed').
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this activity log entry was created.

### `hrm_tracker_timers`

Active timer entry for employees tracking time in real-time. Each
employee can have at most one active timer at any given time. The timer
records the project (required) and optional task being worked on, along
with description and start timestamp. When stopped, a timelog is created
from this timer state. Organization-scoped for multi-tenancy isolation.

**Key constraints**:
- One active timer per employee (@@unique([employee_id, deleted_at]))
- Project reference is mandatory
- Task reference is optional but must belong to the selected project
- Timer state is ephemeral and automatically converted to timelog on stop

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `employee_id`: Employee who owns this timer. [hrm_tracker_employees.id](#hrm_tracker_employees).
- `project_id`: Project being tracked (required). [hrm_tracker_projects.id](#hrm_tracker_projects).
- `task_id`
  > Optional task being tracked (must belong to selected project). {@link
  > hrm_tracker_tasks.id}.
- `organization_id`
  > Organization context for multi-tenancy isolation. {@link
  > hrm_tracker_organizations.id}.
- `description`: Optional description of the work being tracked.
- `start_timestamp`: When the timer was started (ISO 8601 datetime).
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (null = active, non-null = deleted).

### `hrm_tracker_activity_log_details`

Key-value pairs extracted from JSON details field for proper 1NF
compliance. Stores structured audit details as separate rows instead of
JSON strings.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `hrm_tracker_activity_log_id`: Parent activity log's [hrm_tracker_activity_logs.id](#hrm_tracker_activity_logs).
- `key`: Key name for the detail (e.g., 'old_status', 'new_status', 'changed_by').
- `value`: Value for the detail.

Guest registration endpoint allows unauthenticated users to create a guest account. Guests can sign up using email and password, which enables them to later join organizations.

**Authentication Flow**: When a guest registers, the system generates a unique device fingerprint if not provided, creates a guest record with encrypted password hash using BCrypt, and sets the email address. The created_at and updated_at timestamps are automatically populated with the current timestamp. The guest then receives authentication tokens to access the system before joining an organization.

**Database Integration**: The operation inserts into the hrm_tracker_guests table with the device_fingerprint, email, password_hash, and default timestamps. Upon successful registration, the guest can use the refresh endpoint to renew their session tokens.

**Security Considerations**: Passwords must be encrypted using BCrypt before storage. The system validates email format and uniqueness before creating the guest record. The deleted_at field remains NULL for active guest accounts.

**Related Operations**: After guest registration, users can use the refresh endpoint to obtain new access tokens. When ready to join an organization, guests can upgrade to member status.

Token refresh endpoint allows guests to obtain new access tokens using a valid refresh token without re-authenticating. This is essential for maintaining session continuity without requiring users to re-register.

**Authentication Flow**: When a guest's access token expires, they can use their refresh token to obtain new tokens. The system validates the refresh token, checks its expiration, and generates new access and refresh token pairs. The guest record's updated_at timestamp is refreshed to reflect the token renewal activity.

**Database Integration**: The operation updates the hrm_tracker_guests table's updated_at field with the current timestamp. The refresh token validation ensures that only legitimate token renewals are processed. If the refresh token is invalid or expired, the request is rejected.

**Security Considerations**: Refresh tokens must be validated for authenticity and expiration before issuing new tokens. The system maintains token rotation security by invalidating old refresh tokens when new ones are issued. All token operations use secure cryptographic practices.

Store hashed password, create initial member record with status 'pending', generate verification token with 24-hour expiry, send email with verification link containing token, return session tokens only after email verification is completed.
operations.description:
Member Registration Endpoint

This endpoint creates a new member account for users who wish to join the system. The registration process follows a secure multi-step workflow designed to verify email ownership before activating the account.

## Registration Workflow

1. **Account Creation**: User submits email address and password. The password is securely hashed using BCrypt algorithm before storage.

2. **Initial Record State**: A member record is created with status 'pending' and email_verified set to false. This prevents unauthorized access until email ownership is verified.

3. **Email Verification**: A unique verification token is generated with a 24-hour expiration period. This token is sent to the user's email address as part of a verification link.

4. **Activation Requirement**: The account remains in 'pending' status until the user clicks the verification link and the token is validated. Only after successful email verification does the account status change to 'active'.

## Security Considerations

- Passwords are stored as BCrypt hashes, never in plain text
- Verification tokens have short expiration (24 hours) to limit abuse
- Each member record tracks creation and update timestamps for audit purposes
- Email addresses must be unique across the system
- The member's display name is captured at registration for profile identification
- The 'phone' field is optional and stored as a varchar field

## Database Integration

The hrm_tracker_members table stores the member's core information including:
- id (UUID primary key)
- email (unique constraint enforced)
- password_hash (BCrypt hashed password)
- display_name (user's chosen display name)
- phone (optional contact information)
- status ('pending' initially, becomes 'active' after verification)
- email_verified (boolean flag)
- created_at, updated_at timestamps
- deleted_at (for soft delete support)

The hrm_tracker_member_email_verifications table stores verification tokens with expiration timestamps, linking back to the member record via member_id foreign key.

## Post-Registration Flow

After successful registration, the endpoint returns a session object containing access and refresh tokens. However, the member account remains in 'pending' status until email verification is completed. This ensures that only legitimate email owners can fully activate their accounts.

requestBody.description: Member registration request with email, password, and display name.

responseBody.description: Member session with access and refresh tokens after successful registration.

operations.specification: Validate member credentials against stored password hash, create new session with JWT tokens if valid, update session metadata with IP address and user agent, store session tokens in database, return tokens to client for subsequent authenticated requests.
operations.description:
Member Login Endpoint

This endpoint authenticates member users by validating their email address and password credentials against the stored account information in the database.

## Authentication Process

1. **Credential Validation**: User submits their registered email address and password. The system retrieves the member record by email and validates the provided password against the stored BCrypt hash.

2. **Account Status Check**: Before granting access, the system verifies the account status is 'active' and email has been verified. Deactivated accounts or unverified accounts are rejected.

3. **Session Creation**: Upon successful authentication, a new session record is created in the hrm_tracker_member_sessions table. This record stores:
   - Access token (JWT for API authentication)
   - Refresh token (JWT for token renewal)
   - Client IP address for security auditing
   - User agent string from the client device
   - Expiration timestamps for both tokens
   - Last activity timestamp

4. **Token Issuance**: The endpoint returns both access and refresh tokens to the client. The access token is used for immediate API requests, while the refresh token can be used later to obtain new access tokens without requiring re-authentication.

## Security Implementation

- Password validation uses BCrypt hash comparison
- Session tokens are stored in the database with IP and user agent metadata
- Token expiration is tracked with expires_at timestamps
- Session revocation is supported via revoked_at timestamp
- The last_activity_at field enables session validity checking
- Failed login attempts can be tracked by monitoring this endpoint

## Database Integration

The hrm_tracker_members table contains the user's credentials and status information:
- id (UUID primary key)
- email (unique identifier for login)
- password_hash (BCrypt hashed password for validation)
- status ('active' required for login)
- email_verified (must be true for authentication)
- created_at, updated_at, deleted_at timestamps

The hrm_tracker_member_sessions table stores active session records with:
- access_token and refresh_token strings
- ip and user_agent client metadata
- created_at, expires_at timestamps
- revoked_at (nullable for active sessions)
- last_activity_at for session health monitoring

## Post-Login Expectations

After successful login, the client must include the access token in the Authorization header of all subsequent API requests. The refresh token should be stored securely and used only when the access token expires or needs renewal.

requestBody.description: Member login request with email and password credentials.

responseBody.description: Member session with access and refresh tokens after successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate refresh token against database session record, verify token hasn't expired or been revoked, generate new access token with extended expiration, update session's last_activity_at timestamp, return new access token in response, invalidate refresh token if used once (optional security approach).
operations.description:
Token Refresh Endpoint

This endpoint allows authenticated members to obtain new access tokens using their valid refresh token, enabling extended session duration without requiring re-authentication.

## Token Refresh Workflow

1. **Token Validation**: The client submits their current refresh token to this endpoint. The system retrieves the session record from hrm_tracker_member_sessions table and validates:
   - The refresh token matches the stored token
   - The session has not been revoked (revoked_at is NULL)
   - The token has not expired (expires_at is in the future)
   - The session is associated with an active member account

2. **Access Token Generation**: Upon successful validation, a new access token is generated with an updated expiration time. The refresh token may be renewed or remain the same depending on security policy.

3. **Session Update**: The session record is updated with the new last_activity_at timestamp to reflect recent activity. This helps track active sessions and can be used for session cleanup procedures.

4. **Response Delivery**: The endpoint returns the new access token (and optionally a new refresh token) to the client for continued authenticated access.

## Security Considerations

- Refresh tokens have longer expiration times than access tokens but still expire eventually
- Session revocation (via revoked_at) immediately invalidates all session tokens
- IP address tracking can help detect suspicious token usage patterns
- User agent monitoring provides additional session validation context
- The last_activity_at field enables implementating session timeout logic
- Optional single-use refresh tokens can be implemented for enhanced security

## Database Integration

The hrm_tracker_member_sessions table provides the validation context:
- refresh_token (string field for lookup)
- revoked_at (NULL indicates active session)
- expires_at (token expiration timestamp)
- ip and user_agent (client metadata for validation)
- created_at, last_activity_at (session lifecycle tracking)

The associated hrm_tracker_members record must have status 'active' and email_verified true for the refresh to succeed.

## Post-Refresh Expectations

After successfully refreshing the access token, the client should use the new access token for subsequent API requests. The old access token becomes invalid immediately. If the refresh token itself has expired or been revoked, the client must re-authenticate using the login endpoint.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request with current refresh token.

responseBody.description: New access token after successful refresh token validation.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated member's global profile information.

This operation returns the complete profile details of the currently authenticated member account. The profile data includes the global display name, avatar image URL, contact phone number, and email verification status that is shared across all organizations the member belongs to.

The operation requires valid authentication and returns only the profile data for the authenticated member. No other member profiles can be accessed through this endpoint. This aligns with the business rule that each member has a single global profile consistent across all organizations they belong to.

All profile fields returned by this endpoint are part of the global profile shared across organizations, including display name, avatar image reference, phone number, and email verification status. Department, position, and employment type information are organization-specific and are not included in this global profile response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve the authenticated member's profile from hrm_tracker_members table using the member ID from authentication context.
Return the global profile fields: display_name, avatar_url, phone, email_verified, created_at, updated_at, email, status.
Do not return password_hash or any sensitive authentication data.
Ensure the operation uses the authenticated member's ID derived from the security context, not a path parameter.
Return 404 if the member account is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null).

responseBody.description: Member's global profile data including display name, avatar, phone, and email verification status

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's global profile information.

This endpoint allows members to update their own profile data, which includes their display name, avatar image URL, and contact phone number. The profile is global and shared across all organizations the member belongs to.

Only the authenticated member can update their own profile. Members cannot update other users' profile information. The display name must be provided and should be appropriate for organizational use. The avatar URL should point to an accessible image resource. The phone number is optional but should follow standard formatting if provided.

Profile updates are not tracked in activity logs - changes to profile information do not generate audit records according to business rules. The global profile consistency rule ensures that profile changes are immediately visible across all organizational contexts the member belongs to.

If the member leaves an organization, their profile data persists independently and remains accessible when they join other organizations.
operations.name: updateProfile
operations.specification:
Update the authenticated member's global profile in the hrm_tracker_members table.

1. Extract the authenticated member ID from the request context (JWT token or session).
2. Load the current member record from hrm_tracker_members table using the member ID.
3. Validate that the authenticated member ID matches the target member record (prevent unauthorized updates).
4. Apply partial updates for provided fields: display_name, avatar_url, phone.
5. Validate the display_name is provided and not empty.
6. Validate avatar_url format if provided (must be valid URL string).
7. Update the updated_at timestamp to current time.
8. Save the updated member record to the database.
9. Return the updated member profile data.

No activity log entry is generated for profile updates per business rules.

responseBody.description: Updated member profile information

requestBody.description: Profile update request data

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of active authentication sessions.

This operation provides advanced search and filtering capabilities for member sessions stored in the hrm_tracker_member_sessions table. It allows administrators and authorized members to view session history, identify active sessions, and monitor access patterns.

The endpoint supports filtering by member identifier, date range (created_at, expires_at), IP address, and session status (active/revoked). Pagination enables handling large result sets efficiently. Response includes session summary information with token metadata and connection details for security auditing and access management purposes.
operations.name: index

Filter by member_id for specific user's sessions, date ranges for created_at and expires_at, ip address matching, and revoked_at null check for active status. responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for session filtering

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific JWT session token.

This operation fetches a single session record from the member_sessions table, providing complete visibility into the session's metadata including connection details and activity timeline. The returned data includes client connection information and session lifecycle timestamps.

Session data is highly sensitive and should only be accessible to system administrators or security auditors. The operation supports security investigations, compliance audits, and troubleshooting by providing a complete audit trail of active and revoked sessions.

This endpoint is designed for administrative use cases only. Regular API authentication should not require retrieving session records directly—client applications should use the standard access token refresh flow instead.

operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_member_sessions table by id (UUID).
Return complete session record including access_token, refresh_token, ip, user_agent, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at, and last_activity_at.
If session not found, return 404 Not Found.
If session is revoked (revoked_at present), return 403 Forbidden.
Apply organization-level authorization to ensure caller has permission to view session data for the associated member.

operations.description:
Update organization system configuration settings.

This operation allows authorized users to update system configuration settings stored as key-value pairs per organization. Configuration settings include fiscal start month, currency, timezone, and other organizational preferences.

The operation accepts individual configuration key updates and applies them to the organization's configuration records. All updates are applied in a single transaction, ensuring consistency across the configuration store.

Each configuration update requires validation of both the configuration key and its value format. Invalid keys or malformed values will cause the entire transaction to roll back, maintaining data integrity.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update hrm_tracker_system_configs records for the authenticated user's organization context.

1. Retrieve the organization ID from the authenticated user's session.
2. For each configuration update in the request body:
   - Validate the configuration key against the predefined set of valid keys.
   - Validate the configuration value format (e.g., timezone, currency).
   - Update the value field in hrm_tracker_system_configs.
   - Update the updated_at timestamp to the current time.
3. Apply all updates within a single database transaction.
4. If any validation fails or database update encounters an error, roll back the entire transaction.
5. Return the updated configuration records for all successfully updated keys.
6. Handle edge cases: key not found, invalid key format, value validation failure.

responseBody.description: Updated organization configuration settings

requestBody.description: Array of configuration key-value pairs to update

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific organization configuration by its key.

This operation fetches a single configuration setting from the system configuration table. The configuration is scoped to the organization of the authenticated actor. Only the configuration key and its stored value are returned.

Configuration values are stored as strings to support flexible data types (e.g., 'true' for booleans, '2024-01-01' for dates). The application layer is responsible for parsing and type conversion based on the configuration key.

operations.description:
Create a new system configuration entry for the current organization.

This operation allows any authenticated member to add a new configuration key-value pair to the organization's system configuration settings. Each configuration key must be unique within an organization, and the value is stored as a string for maximum flexibility.

The configuration entry is automatically associated with the organization context of the authenticated user's active session. The system enforces uniqueness of keys within each organization, preventing duplicate configuration entries.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new system configuration record in hrm_tracker_system_configs table.

1. Extract hrm_tracker_organization_id from the user's active session context.
2. Validate that the key is not empty and follows naming conventions.
3. Check for existing configuration with the same key in the same organization to prevent duplicates.
4. Create the configuration record with provided key, value, and organization context.
5. Return the created configuration with id, key, value, and timestamps.

responseBody.description: Created system configuration entry

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for database migration versions including version identifier filtering, applied date ranges, and rollback version status. It allows administrators to browse the history of applied schema migrations and identify which versions are currently active or have been rolled back.

The system versions table tracks all schema migrations applied to the database, providing a complete audit trail of schema changes over time. Each record includes the version identifier, timestamp when it was applied, and optionally references the previous version for rollback tracking.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_system_versions table with pagination and filtering.
Apply search filters on version identifier, applied_at date range, and rollback_version presence.

Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of organizations.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities including name filtering, status filtering, and administrative organization listing. Users can filter organizations by name pattern, status (active, archived, deleted), and search by owner email or name.

This operation respects the multi-tenancy foundation where users can only see organizations they belong to through employee records. Organization owners and administrators have access to all organizations for management purposes. The response includes organization summary information optimized for list displays.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_organizations table with pagination and filtering.
Apply search filters on name, status, and owner information.
Filter organizations by the currently logged-in user's organization membership.
Apply soft-delete filtering (exclude deleted_at != NULL).
Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets.
