operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific organization.

This operation fetches the complete organization record by its unique identifier. The response includes all organization details such as name, description, currency configuration, timezone settings, fiscal year configuration, status, and timestamps. The operation is scoped to the user's currently selected organization context, ensuring users only access organizations they belong to.

All organization data is isolated per organization. Users with multi-organization membership will only see data from their currently selected organization context. The organization owner (user who created the organization) has full administrative access to all organization settings.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_organizations table by primary key (id).
Filter by user's current organization context from session authentication.
Return organization details including name, description, logo_image_uri, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, status, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.
Return 404 if organization not found or user lacks access to this organization context.

responseBody.description: Detailed organization information including all configuration fields

operations.description:
Create a new organization entity.

This operation creates a new organization that serves as the primary container for all organizational data including employees, projects, departments, contracts, time tracking, and reporting data. When an organization is created, the authenticated user automatically becomes the organization owner with full administrative privileges.

The organization is the central unit for multi-tenancy — all data and operations are strictly isolated within the organization boundary. The organization owner has complete control over organization settings, member management, and data access.

After creation, the user can begin inviting employees, creating departments, setting up projects, and configuring other organizational settings. The organization settings including currency, timezone, and fiscal start month establish the operational context for all subsequent data and reports.

This operation is available only to authenticated members during their initial sign-up or when establishing additional organizations. Users must select an organization context after creation to begin working within that organization.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new organization record in hrm_tracker_organizations table.

- Assign authenticated member as owner via owner_member_id
- Validate organization name uniqueness within hrm_tracker_organizations
- Set status to 'active' by default
- Initialize fiscal_start_month with provided value (1-12)
- Store timezone as string (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul')
- Store currency as ISO code (e.g., 'USD', 'KRW')
- Generate created_at and updated_at timestamps
- Return complete organization record including auto-generated fields
- Enforce multi-tenancy isolation from creation
- Set deleted_at to null (no soft-delete at creation)

responseBody.description: Created organization record with all details

requestBody.description: Organization creation request with all required and optional fields

operations.description:
Update organization settings for the specified organization.

This operation allows organization administrators to modify core organizational settings including the organization name, description, logo image URI, currency code, timezone, and fiscal year start month. All updates are scoped to the current organization context and require proper authorization checks.

## Authorization and Security

Only authenticated members with appropriate permissions can update organization settings. The operation validates that:
- The user belongs to the target organization
- The user has sufficient privileges to modify organization settings
- All updates respect multi-tenancy boundaries

## Business Rules and Validation

- Organization name must be unique across all organizations and cannot be empty
- Currency code must follow ISO 4217 standard format (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW)
- Timezone must be a valid IANA timezone identifier
- Fiscal start month must be between 1 and 12
- Logo image URI must be a valid URI format if provided

## Related Operations

- `GET /organizations/{organizationId}` must be pre-executed to retrieve current organization data before making updates
- `PATCH /organizations` can be used to search and list organizations
- `DELETE /organizations/{organizationId}` permanently removes an organization

## Error Handling

Common error scenarios include:
- Organization not found
- Unauthorized access (user not in organization or insufficient permissions)
- Validation failures (invalid currency, timezone, or other format errors)
- Concurrent update conflicts
- Unique constraint violations (duplicate organization name)
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update organization settings in hrm_tracker_organizations table.
Validate organization ownership and permissions before update.
Check unique constraint on organization name.
Apply data validation for currency (ISO 4217), timezone (IANA), fiscal_start_month (1-12), and logo_image_uri (valid URI format).
Return updated organization record.

responseBody.description: Updated organization record with all settings

requestBody.description: Organization update request with settings to modify

operations.description:
Permanently delete an organization and all its associated data.

This operation permanently removes an organization record and all related data including employees, projects, departments, contracts, timelogs, timesheets, activity logs, and pending invitations. According to the data retention policy, this deletion is irreversible and immediate—the data is purged from the system with no backup or soft-delete mechanism.

Before deletion can proceed, the system validates that all pending timesheets are resolved (approved or rejected), all employee contracts have end dates set, and there are no pending invitations. If any of these conditions are not met, the deletion request is rejected with a clear explanation of what remains unresolved.

Only organization owners can perform this operation. The operation does not affect the owner's global profile or other organizations they may belong to.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_organizations table by id for organization deletion.
Validate organization deletion eligibility: ensure all pending timesheets are resolved, all employee contracts have end dates, and no pending invitations exist.
Check that the requesting member is the organization owner (hrm_tracker_organizations.owner_member_id).
If any validation fails, return appropriate error response.
If validation passes, delete the organization record from hrm_tracker_organizations table.
Cascade deletion handles related employee, project, department, contract, timelog, timesheet, activity, and invitation records.
Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

operations.description: This endpoint is intentionally unavailable. According to the hrmTracker business rules, pending invitations are created automatically by the system when inviting employees - they cannot be manually created via API POST. The system enforces that only the internal invitation workflow can generate pending invitations, ensuring proper authorization checks and audit trail. Any attempt to manually create an invitation would bypass these critical business rules.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: This operation is intentionally disabled. The hrmTracker system strictly prohibits manual creation of pending invitations via API endpoints. According to the business rules defined in sections 274, 275, 437, 568, 573, and 574, pending invitations are automatically generated by the system when authorized users trigger the employee invitation workflow. Manual POST requests to /invitations would violate these core business principles and must be rejected with a 405 Method Not Allowed status.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of pending invitations with filtering and sorting capabilities.

This operation provides comprehensive list access to pending invitations, supporting advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination. It enables administrators to search for specific invitations by email address, filter by status, and navigate through large result sets efficiently.

The API supports flexible querying through the request body, allowing clients to combine multiple filter criteria and specify sorting preferences for optimal data browsing experience.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_pending_invitations table with pagination and filtering.
Apply search filters on email, status, invited_at date range, and organization context.
Support sorting by invited_at, email, and status.
Return cursor-based or offset-based pagination for large result sets.
Filter by organization_id from user's organization context.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of pending invitation summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific pending invitation.

This operation fetches the complete details of a pending invitation, including the organization context, inviter information, invitation email, status, and any message included in the invitation. It is used by authorized employees to view invitation details before resolution through signup.

The operation requires the calling member to have employee management permission within the organization context. This ensures that only authorized personnel can view pending invitations, maintaining data security and preventing unauthorized access to invitation data.

The response includes the full invitation record with all metadata, allowing administrators to verify invitation details, check status, and understand the context of the pending onboarding request.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_tracker_pending_invitations table by invitationId.
Include organization_id, invited_by_member_id, email, message, role_name, department_name, invited_at, resolved_at, status, and token fields.
Join with hrm_tracker_organizations to include organization name and context.
Join with hrm_tracker_members to include inviter details when invited_by_member_id is present.
Return 404 if invitation not found.
Return 403 if calling member lacks employee management permission for the organization.

responseBody.description: Complete pending invitation details including organization context and inviter information

operations.description:
Permanently delete a pending invitation from the system.

This operation completely removes a pending invitation record from the hrm_tracker_pending_invitations table. The operation is performed when an authorized user decides to cancel an invitation that has not yet been accepted by the target user.

Security considerations: Only users with the employee:manage permission within the organization can cancel pending invitations. Unauthorized attempts will result in a 403 Forbidden response.

Related operations:
- POST /hrmTracker/member/invitations - Create new pending invitations
- GET /hrmTracker/member/invitations - List pending invitations for an organization

Once cancelled, the invitation cannot be restored and any future attempts to use it for onboarding will fail. If a new invitation is needed, a fresh invitation must be created.
operations.name: cancel
operations.specification:
Cancel a pending invitation by setting its status to 'cancelled'.

1. Load pending invitation by id from hrm_tracker_pending_invitations table
2. Verify the invitation exists and has status 'pending'
3. Check that calling user has employee:manage permission for the organization
4. Update invitation status to 'cancelled'
5. Return the updated invitation record

Edge cases:
- Invitation already cancelled/accepted/expired: return 409 Conflict
- User lacks permission: return 403 Forbidden
- Invalid invitation id: return 404 Not Found

operations.description:
Permanently delete a pending invitation.

This operation removes a pending invitation record from the system. Unlike soft-delete operations that mark records as deleted, this delete permanently removes the invitation data. The deleted invitation cannot be recovered.

Authorization:
- Only authenticated members with appropriate permissions can delete pending invitations
- Members can only delete invitations associated with their organization
- The invited_by_member_id reference must exist on the invitation

When a pending invitation is deleted:
- The invitation record is permanently removed from the database
- No email notification is sent to the invited person
- No employee record is created from the deleted invitation
- Any pending signup attempts using the invitation token will fail
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Delete pending invitation by ID. Verify user belongs to the organization that sent the invitation. Check that the invitation exists and has status 'pending'. Permanently remove the invitation record from the database. Do NOT soft-delete — use hard delete with CASCADE delete to related records.

operations.description:
Retrieve organization configuration settings for the current organization context.

This operation returns the organization's fiscal start month, currency code, timezone, display name, and logo URL. It is designed for authorized users who need to view current organizational preferences and configuration.

Security and Permissions:
- Requires the org:manage permission to access organization settings
- The operation always retrieves settings for the organization in the current context
- Analysis sections confirm that organization owners can edit settings, while other roles with org:manage can view settings

Database Entity:
- Uses the hrm_tracker_organization_settings table which stores configuration for each organization
- Returns the single active settings record for the current organization context
- Fields include fiscal_start_month (1-12), currency (ISO 4217 code), timezone (IANA name), name (display name), and logo_url (image URL)
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_organization_settings table for the current organization context.
Return fiscal_start_month, currency, timezone, name, and logo_url fields.
Ensure the operation uses the organization ID from the current session context.

responseBody.description: Organization settings including fiscal start month, currency, timezone, name, and logo URL

operations.description:
Update organization configuration settings.

This operation allows organization owners to modify key configuration settings including the organization name, description, logo image URI, currency code, timezone, and fiscal year start month.

Security and Authorization: This endpoint is restricted to users with the owner role in the current organization. Users with other roles (manager, employee, or custom roles) cannot modify these settings. The organization context is derived from the user's active organization selection in the session.

Settings Fields:
- name: Organization display name
- description: Organization description
- logo_image_uri: URI/URL pointing to the organization logo image
- currency: Three-letter currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW)
- timezone: IANA timezone identifier (e.g., Asia/Seoul, America/New_York)
- fiscal_start_month: Integer month (1-12) marking the fiscal year start

Validation: All field updates are validated against domain constraints. The name field must remain globally unique. The logo_image_uri must be a valid URI if provided.
operations.name: updateSettings
operations.specification: Update organization settings in hrm_tracker_organizations table based on user's active organization context. Fetch organization by organization context from session, verify user has owner role, then update fields: name, description, logo_image_uri, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month. Apply validation for uniqueness and URI format. Return updated organization record with full details.

responseBody.description: Updated organization settings with all fields

requestBody.description: Settings update payload with configurable organization fields

operations.description:
Assign a role to an employee within their organization.

This operation assigns a specific role to an employee, replacing any existing role assignment. The employee must belong to the same organization as the user performing the assignment. Only users with employee:manage permission or organization owners can perform this operation.

The operation is fully auditable: the system records who performed the assignment, when it occurred, and the prior and new role assignments in the activity log. The role assignment takes effect immediately for all subsequent operations and permissions checks.
operations.name: assign
operations.specification:
Assign a role to an employee by updating the hrm_tracker_employees.role_id field with the provided role_id from the request body.

- Fetch employee by ID and verify it belongs to the requesting user's organization
- Fetch role by ID and verify it belongs to the same organization
- Check authorization: only owners or users with employee:manage permission can perform this operation
- Update the employee's role_id to the new role_id
- Record the role assignment change in the activity log with details about who performed the change, when, and the prior and new roles
- Return the updated employee information including the new role assignment

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the employee to assign a role to
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: Role assignment request payload

operations.description:
Assign permissions to a custom role within the organization.

This operation allows organization owners to grant additional permissions to custom roles they have created. The target role must be a custom role (is_custom = true); built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be modified through this API. When permissions are assigned, all employees with that role immediately inherit the new permissions.

Permission codes follow the format `{resource}:{action}` and must be one of the allowed values: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view.

Only users with org:manage permission can assign permissions to roles. Authorization is enforced at the organization level—users can only modify roles within their own organization.

After assignment, the new permissions are immediately active for all employees assigned to this role. Existing employees with the role will gain access to the newly assigned permissions without requiring reassignment.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Assign permissions to a custom role by inserting records into hrm_tracker_permissions table.

1. Validate target role exists in hrm_tracker_roles and belongs to the requesting organization
2. Reject if role is not custom (is_custom = false) — built-in roles cannot be edited
3. Validate each permission code matches allowed values
4. Insert permission assignments with hrm_tracker_role_id = roleId and permission = code
5. Enforce composite unique constraint on (hrm_tracker_role_id, permission)
6. Return 201 Created on success, 400 for validation errors, 404 for non-existent/custom role, 403 for unauthorized access

responseBody.description: Success confirmation with assigned permission count

requestBody.description: Permission codes to assign to the role

operations.description:
Remove a specific permission from a role within an organization.

This operation removes a permission assignment from a role, effectively revoking that permission from all employees assigned to the role. The permission is removed from the role's permission set, and the change takes effect immediately for all employees with that role.

**Authorization**:

- Only organization owners can remove permissions from roles
- The role must belong to the organization of the currently authenticated user
- Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot have their permissions modified

**Permission Constraints**:

- The permission must exist and be assigned to the specified role
- Attempting to remove a permission that is not assigned to the role will fail
- The role must be a custom role (is_custom = true); built-in roles are immutable

**Business Logic**:

- When a permission is removed, all employees with that role immediately lose that permission
- The system enforces permissions at the time of each operation based on the user's current role assignment
- Deletion of the permission assignment is permanent and cannot be undone
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a permission assignment from a role.
1. Verify organization ownership authorization (only org owners can modify roles)
2. Verify the role exists and belongs to the organization
3. Verify the role is custom (is_custom = true) - built-in roles are immutable
4. Verify the permission exists and is assigned to the role via hrm_tracker_role_permissions junction table
5. Delete the hrm_tracker_role_permissions record (cascades to hrm_tracker_permissions if last assignment)
6. Return no content on success, or error if any validation fails

parameters.description: Target role's unique identifier. Must belong to the organization of the authenticated user.
parameters.name: roleId

parameters.description: Permission code to remove (e.g., project:manage, time:approve). Must be assigned to the role.
parameters.name: permission

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of employee records.

This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for employee records within the current organization context, supporting filtering by status (active/deactivated), department, employment type, and position. The response includes employee summary information optimized for list displays and pagination.

The operation enforces organization-level data isolation by requiring the organization ID in the path parameter, ensuring users only see employees from their currently selected organization.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_employees table with pagination and filtering.
Apply search filters on status, department_id, employment_type, and position (using trigram matching for partial matches).
Join with hrm_tracker_members for user details.
Join with hrm_tracker_departments for department name.
Join with hrm_tracker_roles for role name.
Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets.
Respect soft delete filter: exclude records with non-null deleted_at.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of employee summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for employee list

operations.description:
Create a new employee record linked to an organization.

This endpoint allows authorized users to add a new employee to the organization by linking an existing user account with organization-specific details such as employment type, position, and optional role/department assignments. The employee record becomes active upon creation.

**Security and Authorization:**
- Requires employee:manage permission to create new employee records
- Employee must belong to exactly one organization
- Employee status is set to 'active' by default upon creation
- Deactivated employees (status='deactivated') retain historical data but cannot log time or submit timesheets

**Business Rules:**
- Employment type must be one of the predefined values: 'full-time', 'part-time', 'contractor', 'intern'
- Status must be 'active' or 'deactivated'
- Role and department are optional but must belong to the same organization as the employee
- Employee records maintain audit trail through created_at and updated_at timestamps

**Relationships:**
- Links to hrm_tracker_members (user) for authentication context
- Links to hrm_tracker_organizations for data isolation
- Optional links to hrm_tracker_roles and hrm_tracker_departments
- If referenced role or department is deleted, the foreign key is set to NULL

**Error Conditions:**
- Duplicate error when same user is already assigned as employee in the organization
- Validation error for invalid employment_type or status values
- Reference errors if role_id or department_id belongs to different organization
- Department deletion behavior: when department is deleted, employee.department_id becomes NULL but employee record remains active
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create employee record by inserting into hrm_tracker_employees table.

1. Input validation:
   - employment_type must be one of: 'full-time', 'part-time', 'contractor', 'intern'
   - status must be one of: 'active', 'deactivated'
   - role_id and department_id must belong to same organization as employee
   - Check for duplicate: organization_id + user_id must be unique

2. Database operation:
   - Insert into hrm_tracker_employees with provided fields
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
   - Set deleted_at to NULL for active employee

3. Return created employee with complete object including generated timestamps

responseBody.description: Created employee record with all fields

requestBody.description: Employee creation data including organization, user, employment type, and optional role/department

operations.description:
Update an existing employee record within an organization.

This operation updates the details of an employee including their assigned role, department, status (active/deactivated), employment type, and position title. All updates are scoped to the organization context of the authenticated employee.

Security & Permissions: Only users with employee:manage permission can perform this operation. The system validates that the target employee belongs to the authenticated organization and that role and department assignments exist within the same organization.

Business Rules:
- If department_id is set to null, the employee loses their department assignment (as per 'Department Assignment Is Optional for Employees')
- Setting department_id to an invalid department or one belonging to a different organization is rejected
- If the role_id is changed, the employee immediately inherits all permissions assigned to that role
- Deactivated employees (status='deactivated') retain their historical data but lose the ability to log time or submit timesheets

Relationships & Dependencies:
- The role must belong to the same organization as the employee
- The department must belong to the same organization as the employee
- An employee can only be assigned to a role that exists within the same organization

Edge Cases:
- Attempting to assign a role or department from a different organization is rejected
- Attempting to deactivate an employee does not delete their historical records (timelogs, timesheets, tasks)
- Updating an employee with status='deactivated' preserves all historical data while preventing future time logging
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_employees by id and verify organization context matches authenticated session.
Update the employee record with provided fields: role_id, department_id, status, employment_type, position.
Validate that role_id (if provided) belongs to the same organization.
Validate that department_id (if provided) belongs to the same organization.
If status='deactivated', ensure deleted_at is set to current timestamp.
If status='active', ensure deleted_at is set to NULL.
Update updated_at to current timestamp.
Return the complete updated employee record.

responseBody.description: Updated employee record with all current values

requestBody.description: Employee update request with optional fields for role, department, status, employment type, and position

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of roles within the current organization.

This operation allows organization owners and authorized users to query roles defined in their organization. Roles are the core access control mechanism in hrmTracker, where each role is assigned to employees and grants a specific set of permissions.

Roles in hrmTracker come in two types: built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) that are system-defined and cannot be deleted, and custom roles that organizations can create to match their specific permission requirements. This endpoint allows filtering by role type, searching by name, and viewing both built-in and custom roles in a unified interface.

The response includes essential role information optimized for list displays, such as role name, description, whether it's a custom or built-in role, and if it's set as the default role for new employees. This enables administrators to quickly assess available roles and decide which to assign during employee onboarding or role audits.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_roles table filtered by the current organization context.
Apply filters for role name, is_custom flag, and is_default status.
Support pagination with offset/limit for large result sets.
Return ISummary view with essential role information.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of role summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Create a new custom role within the organization.

This operation allows organization owners and users with employee:manage permission to define a new custom role with a unique name and assign one or more permissions. Custom roles supplement the built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) and enable fine-grained access control tailored to the organization's structure.

Each role must have a name that is unique within the organization, cannot reuse built-in role names, and must be assigned at least one permission. The role is created with the current timestamp and no employees are assigned by default. Role assignments to employees are performed via separate role assignment endpoints.

Role change events are automatically logged in the activity log with details of who performed the change, when, and what the prior and new roles were.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new role record with name, description, is_custom=true, and assigned permissions.

1. Validate: organization context from member actor, employee:manage or owner permission.
2. Check: role name must be unique within organization (no duplicate name).
3. Check: role name must not match built-in role names (Owner, Manager, Employee).
4. Validate: at least one permission is assigned.
5. Create role with is_custom=true, is_default=false.
6. Insert into hrm_tracker_role_permissions to assign permissions.
7. Log activity in hrm_tracker_activity_logs with role change details.
8. Return created role with assigned permissions.

responseBody.description: Created role with assigned permissions

requestBody.description: Role creation parameters including name, optional description, and permission assignments

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific role by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches a single role record using its UUID identifier. Roles are organization-scoped entities that define permission sets for employees. Each organization maintains its own set of roles, which can be either built-in (Owner, Manager, Employee) or custom roles created by organization owners.

The response includes all role details including the name, optional description, whether the role is custom or built-in, and whether it's the default role assigned to newly invited employees. Roles use the `deleted_at` timestamp field for archival purposes, allowing retired roles to be marked without being physically removed from the database.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_roles table by id for single role record.
Include organization context validation to ensure role belongs to current session organization.
Filter out soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL).
Return complete role object with all fields as defined in schema.

responseBody.description: Complete role information

operations.description:
Update an existing role's configuration within the organization.

This endpoint allows organization owners and users with employee:manage permission to modify the name, description, and other properties of a role. You can change a custom role's name, description, and its default status, as well as toggle the is_custom flag for custom roles. This operation performs a full update, so all mutable fields in the request body will overwrite the current values.

Security considerations include that only organization owners or users with employee:manage permission can perform this operation. Built-in roles (is_custom=false) are protected from deletion but can be updated. Custom roles can be updated freely. The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed.

Relationship to underlying entities: This operation modifies the hrm_tracker_roles table, which is organization-scoped and isolated per organization. The updated role affects all employees currently assigned to it through the employee-role mapping table.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Update hrm_tracker_roles table by id with request body fields. Validate organization ownership via hrm_tracker_employee_roles join. Prevent modifying built-in roles (is_custom=false). Ensure custom role name uniqueness within organization. Update only mutable fields: name, description, is_custom, is_default. Automatically refresh updated_at timestamp. Record activity log entry for role change. Validate no employees assigned before soft-delete operations if needed.

responseBody.description: Updated role object

requestBody.description: Role update request with new values for mutable fields

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of departments within the organization.

This operation provides advanced search and filtering capabilities for organizational departments. Users can filter departments by name (partial match), search within a specific parent department, and navigate large result sets through pagination. All departments returned belong to the same organization context of the authenticated user.

Security and authorization: Only users with org:manage permission can access this endpoint. The operation enforces organization-level data isolation, ensuring users only see departments within their assigned organization.

Relationships and hierarchy: The system supports one-level department nesting where departments may optionally have a parent department. The parent filter allows retrieving only direct children of a specified parent department. Department names must be unique within each organization.

Filtering options: Search by partial name match, filter by parent department ID, and apply pagination to control result set size and navigation.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_departments table with pagination and filtering.
Apply search filters on name (LIKE partial match), parent_id, and hrm_tracker_organization_id.

operations.description:

The department name must be unique within the same organization.

Security and Permissions: Only users with the org:manage permission are authorized to create new departments. The system automatically associates the new department with the authenticated user's organization context.

Validation Rules:
- Department name must be unique within the organization
- Parent department (if provided) must belong to the same organization
- Circular parent-child references are prohibited
- Only one level of hierarchy is allowed (no grandchild departments)

This operation supports the standard department management workflow where administrators can organize employees into hierarchical units while maintaining strict data integrity rules.

operations.description:
Update an existing department by ID.

This operation updates the department's name, description, and parent department relationship. It enforces the following business rules:

- Only users with org:manage permission in the department's organization can perform this operation.
- The department name must be unique within its organization. Attempting to set a name that already exists in the same organization will result in a validation error.
- The department hierarchy supports only one level of nesting. A department cannot have more than one parent, and grandchild departments are not allowed.
- The parent department must belong to the same organization as the department being updated. Cross-organization parent-child relationships are prohibited.
- No circular dependencies are allowed in the department structure. Any operation that would create a circular parent-child reference is blocked.
- The parent_id field is optional. Setting it to null places the department at the top level of the hierarchy.

This operation is typically used by administrative users to reorganize the company structure, rename departments, or adjust reporting relationships. It should be used with caution to maintain data integrity and prevent accidental misconfigurations of the organizational hierarchy.

Related operations:

- `GET /hrmTracker/member/departments/{departmentId}` - Retrieve detailed information about a specific department
- `PATCH /hrmTracker/member/departments` - Search and list departments with filters and pagination
- `POST /hrmTracker/member/departments` - Create a new department
- `DELETE /hrmTracker/member/departments/{departmentId}` - Delete a department

Update hrm_tracker_departments record by id.

2. Fetch existing department and validate it exists and is not deleted

4. If parent_id provided, verify it belongs to same organization and no circular reference

operations.description:
Permanently remove a department record from the organization's structure.

This operation permanently deletes the specified department from the system. The deletion is irreversible and immediately removes the department from the organizational hierarchy.

To maintain data integrity, this operation includes a validation check that prevents deletion if any employees are currently assigned to the department. If employees exist, the operation is rejected to avoid orphaned department references.

For departments with assigned employees, the system requires employees to be reassigned or the department to be empty before deletion can proceed. This ensures all employee records maintain valid department associations.

Delete a department record by ID with employee count validation.

2. Check for assigned employees using hrm_tracker_employees.department_id
3. If employees exist, reject with 'department_has_employees' error
4. Perform soft-delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp
5. Set employee.department_id to null for all employees in this department
6. Return deleted department record with updated deleted_at timestamp

Soft-delete is implemented using the deleted_at column. The department
remains in database with timestamp but is excluded from normal queries.

Transaction: Delete department record and nullify employee references atomically.

The endpoint filters historical records by the specified employee identifier and returns them in reverse chronological order with the most recent changes appearing first. Users can navigate through the history using pagination controls to review historical states at any point in time.

Tasks can be created as subtasks of an existing parent task, with only one level of nesting allowed. The assigned employee must already be assigned to the project as a project member. The task includes optional estimated hours, due date, priority, and status fields.

Retrieve detailed information about a specific project member assignment.

The response includes the project member's role (member or project-lead), timestamps for creation and updates, and soft delete status for audit purposes.

The operation enforces strict data isolation based on the authenticated actor's permissions:

- **Employees assigned to the project**: Can view this project member record
- **Project leads**: Can view project member records for their assigned project
- **Other employees within the same organization**: Can view project member records for projects they are assigned to

Access is governed by the `project:view` permission. Deactivated employees retain visibility of their historical project assignments but cannot create new timelogs or tasks on those projects.

The system enforces that employees must be assigned to a project via a ProjectMember record before they can log time to that project. Timelogs associated with a project require a valid ProjectMember association for that employee-project pair. If an employee's membership in a project ends (e.g., due to removal), they can no longer log new timelogs to that project, though existing timelogs are preserved and remain linked to the project through their original ProjectMember association.

Employees can be assigned to multiple projects through multiple ProjectMember records, one per project. Each record is independent and can have a different role (member or project-lead). Create a new timelog entry for the authenticated employee.

Security considerations: Employees can only create timelogs for themselves. The operation requires the employee to be assigned to the selected project (or have project management permission). The project must belong to the same organization context as the employee. Date cannot be in the future and duration must be positive.

Validate that the authenticated employee_id matches the session context, project_id belongs to the same organization, and task_id (if provided) belongs to the selected project. Enforce business rules: date must be today or past, duration must be positive, and employee must be assigned to the project (or have permission). Check for locked timesheet periods before insertion.

responseBody.description: Created timelog entry with all fields

requestBody.description: Timelog creation data including date, duration, project reference, and optional task reference

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of timesheet records.

This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for timesheets across the organization. Users can filter by employee, timesheet status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected), date range, and organization context. The endpoint supports efficient data browsing for time tracking management, payroll processing, and approval workflows.

## Security and Authorization

Access to this endpoint is controlled through role-based permissions:

- Standard employees can only view their own timesheets (when employee_id matches their own record)
- Managers with time:approve permission can view all timesheets in their organization for approval purposes
- Administrators with time:view_all permission can view all timesheets across the organization including historical records

The system enforces data isolation based on the member's organizational context and permission scope. Unauthorized access attempts to view other employees' timesheets without proper permissions are rejected.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_timesheets table with pagination and filtering.
Apply filters for employee_id (if restricted by permissions), status, week_start_date, week_end_date, and organization_id.
Join with hrm_tracker_employees for employee details and hrm_tracker_timesheet_timelogs for timelog aggregation.
Calculate total_hours from associated timelogs.
Return paginated results with timesheet summary information optimized for list displays.
Enforce authorization: members can only view their own timesheets unless they have time:approve or time:view_all permissions.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for timesheet filtering

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timesheet by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches a complete timesheet record, including all associated timelogs, for the specified employee and week. The timesheet contains detailed time tracking information used for payroll processing and billing purposes.

**Authorization Requirements:**
- Users can retrieve their own timesheets
- Users with time:approve permission can view all timesheets across the organization
- Users with time:view_all permission can view timesheet data including locked timelogs

**Timesheet Statuses:**
- `draft`: Timesheet is being created, timelogs can be modified
- `submitted`: Timesheet submitted for approval, timelogs locked from employee edits
- `approved`: Timesheet approved by manager, all timelogs fully locked
- `rejected`: Timesheet rejected for revision, returns to draft status
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_tracker_timesheets table by UUID identifier. Join with hrm_tracker_employees for employee reference and hrm_tracker_organizations for organization context. Include all related timelogs from hrm_tracker_timelogs via hrm_tracker_timesheet_timelogs junction table. Apply authorization checks: user must own the timesheet, have time:approve permission, or have time:view_all permission. Return timesheet with full employee and organization details, approval status, and calculated total hours.

responseBody.description: Complete timesheet record with employee reference, organization context, and approval details

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet record
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for manager approval.

This operation allows employees to submit their draft timesheets for manager review and approval. When a timesheet is submitted, its status changes from 'draft' to 'submitted', making it available for users with time:approve permission to approve or reject.

The submitted timesheet is locked from further employee modifications until it is either approved or rejected by an authorized manager. If rejected, the timesheet returns to 'draft' status for revision and resubmission.

Security:
- Only the employee who owns the timesheet can submit it
- Only timesheets with status 'draft' can be submitted
- Timesheets with already-locked timelogs cannot be submitted
- Organization membership is verified for data isolation

Related operations:
- GET /timesheets/{id} (retrieve a specific timesheet)
- GET /timesheets (list employee's timesheets)
- PATCH /timesheets/{id}/approve (approve a submitted timesheet)
- PATCH /timesheets/{id}/reject (reject a submitted timesheet)
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Submit a draft timesheet by changing its status from 'draft' to 'submitted'.

1. Validate that the authenticated employee matches the timesheet's employee_id
2. Verify the timesheet exists and has status 'draft'
3. Verify the timesheet has no locked timelogs (i.e., it's not part of an already approved timesheet)
4. Update timesheet status to 'submitted'
5. Set submitted_at timestamp to current time
6. Return the updated timesheet record

Implementation notes:
- Enforce organization-based multi-tenancy
- Use transaction to ensure atomic status update
- Return 409 Conflict if timesheet is already submitted or approved
- Return 403 Forbidden if employee doesn't own the timesheet
- Log the submission event for audit trail

responseBody.description: The submitted timesheet record with updated status

requestBody.description: Timesheet submission request

operations.description:
Update an existing timesheet record for an employee.

This operation allows employees to update draft timesheets by modifying the status, recalculating total_hours, or updating the rejection_reason when the timesheet is rejected. Only timesheets in draft status can be updated directly; submitted timesheets must first be rejected by a manager before further edits.

The update operation validates that the timesheet belongs to the employee's organization and follows strict state transition rules. For example, a draft timesheet can be updated with new timelog calculations, but a submitted timesheet cannot be directly modified - it must first be rejected by a manager with a rejection reason.

**State Transitions:**

- Draft → Draft: Employee can update status, total_hours, rejection_reason
- Submitted → Draft: Requires prior rejection with rejection_reason
- Approved/Rejected: Cannot be updated (operation blocked)

**Security:**

- Employees can only update their own timesheets or timesheets within their organization
- Timesheets from other organizations are inaccessible
- All updates are logged with updated_at timestamp
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Query hrm_tracker_timesheets table by id with organization and employee joins. Validate timesheet status is draft or rejected (not approved/submitted). Check employee ownership or organization access. Update status, total_hours, rejection_reason fields with current timestamp. Apply strict state transition validation - reject updates that violate transition rules. Return updated timesheet record.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet record with all fields

requestBody.description: Timesheet update request with updatable fields

operations.description:
Approve a submitted timesheet.

This operation allows users with time:approve permission to approve a submitted timesheet. Upon approval, the timesheet status changes to approved, the reviewed at timestamp is recorded, and the reviewer is logged. All timelogs included in an approved timesheet become locked: employees and even users with time:manage permission cannot edit or delete them. Approved timesheets cannot be modified or rejected after approval.

Security and Permissions:

- Only users with time:approve permission can approve timesheets
- Only timesheets in submitted status can be approved
- The timesheet must belong to the same organization as the requesting user
- Approving a timesheet with no timelogs is blocked

Status Transitions:

- draft → submitted (employee submits)
- submitted → approved (manager approves) - this operation
- submitted → draft (manager rejects with reason)
- approved, rejected → no further transitions

 Related Operations:

- POST /timesheets/{timesheetId}/reject — Reject a submitted timesheet with a reason
- GET /timesheets/{timesheetId} — Retrieve timesheet details including approval status
- GET /timesheets — Search timesheets by status for approval workflow
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Approve a submitted timesheet for payroll or billing.

1. Load the target timesheet by ID.
2. Validate organization context matches the timesheet's organization.
3. Verify the user has time:approve permission.
4. Verify the timesheet status is 'submitted'.
5. Verify the timesheet contains at least one timelog.
6. Update status to 'approved', set reviewed_at to current timestamp, and set reviewed_by_member_id to the current user's member ID.
7. Lock all timelogs in the timesheet (set locked flag or mark as non-editable).
8. Return the updated timesheet.

responseBody.description: Approved timesheet with updated status and reviewer information

operations.description:
Reject a submitted timesheet.

This operation allows authorized reviewers to reject a timesheet that is in submitted status. Upon rejection, the timesheet returns to draft status for the employee to revise and resubmit. The rejection reason is stored for audit purposes and to provide clear feedback to the employee.

The operation enforces strict authorization: only users with the time:approve permission can reject timesheets. Users without this authority receive a permission denied error. Additionally, rejection without a reason is blocked, ensuring employees receive clear feedback. Rejection is only allowed on submitted timesheets; draft or already approved/rejected timesheets cannot be processed.

This operation is part of the timesheet approval workflow alongside timesheet approval and submission operations. Rejected timesheets are excluded from approval queues but remain visible to both employees and reviewers for revision and resubmission.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification: Process timesheet rejection for hrm_tracker_timesheets table. Verify user has time:approve permission, confirm timesheet is in submitted status, require rejection reason in request body, update status to draft, set rejection_reason, update reviewed_by_member_id and reviewed_at timestamps. Return updated timesheet record.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet record after rejection

requestBody.description: Rejection reason and metadata

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for approval.

This operation transitions a timesheet from draft status to submitted status, initiating the approval workflow. Only the employee who owns the timesheet can perform this action. The timesheet must contain at least one timelog, there must be no duplicate timesheet for the same week, and no active timer can exist for the employee at submission time.

When successful, the timesheet status changes to submitted, the submitted_at timestamp is recorded, and all associated timelogs become locked to prevent further modifications. The timesheet is then available for review by users with time:approve permission.

This operation enforces strict business rules to maintain data integrity and prevent conflicting time entries.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification: Transition timesheet status from draft to submitted. Validate: (1) timesheet exists and belongs to requesting employee, (2) timesheet has at least one timelog, (3) no duplicate timesheet for same week exists, (4) no active timer for employee. Update status field, set submitted_at timestamp, and lock associated timelogs.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet record after submission

requestBody.description: Request body to submit a draft timesheet for approval

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must exist before submission. The target operation path includes timesheetId, indicating the timesheet was created separately.

operations.description:
Delete a timesheet record from the system.

This operation permanently removes a timesheet (status: draft or submitted) from the database. Timesheets with status approved or rejected are protected and cannot be deleted. Deletion also removes all associated timesheet-timelogjunction records, but timelogs themselves are preserved as they may be referenced elsewhere.

The operation enforces ownership and permission controls:
- Employees can delete their own draft/submitted timesheets
- Users with time:manage permission can delete any timesheet regardless of ownership or status
- Deletion is blocked if the timesheet has status approved or rejected
- Organization deletion is blocked if pending timesheets exist, so this endpoint provides a mechanism to clear pending timesheets to unblock organization deletion

After deletion, the timesheet is permanently removed and cannot be restored. All associated junction records (timesheet-timelog links) are also deleted, but the underlying timelog records remain intact.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Delete a timesheet record by ID. Apply soft-delete using deleted_at timestamp. Ensure timesheet status is draft or submitted (approved/rejected timesheets are protected). Remove all associated hrm_tracker_timesheet_timelogs records via cascade. Preserve underlying timelogs. Enforce authorization: employee can delete own timesheets only; time:manage permission bypasses ownership check.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific activity log entry by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches a single activity log entry from the system's audit trail. The activity log records significant business actions such as employee invitations, deactivations, contract changes, project lifecycle events, task status changes, timesheet workflow actions, and role assignments.

The operation enforces strict authorization: only users with org:manage permission can view activity logs. Users without this permission will receive a permission denied response. All activity log entries are strictly scoped to the currently selected organization context.

The target entity information shows what was affected by the action and includes the entity type (e.g., 'employee', 'contract', 'project', 'task', 'timesheet', 'role', 'pending_invitation', 'organization') and its unique identifier. The action_type field contains one of the predefined action types that were generated by the system in response to business events.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_activity_logs table by UUID ID.
Apply org:manage authorization check before retrieving.
Join with hrm_tracker_members or hrm_tracker_guests for actor details.
Return complete activity log record with all fields including target_entity_type, target_entity_id, action_type, and created_at.

responseBody.description: Complete activity log entry including actor, target, and action details

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of activity log entries with filtering and sorting capabilities.

This operation provides comprehensive filtering options for activity logs, allowing administrators to search by actor (member or guest), target entity type and ID, action type, and date ranges. The activity log serves as an audit trail for accountability, capturing all significant business actions within an organization.

Security and Authorization: Only users with org:manage permission can access activity logs. This ensures that sensitive audit information is restricted to authorized personnel only. The system automatically generates all activity log entries in response to key organizational actions such as employee invitations, contract changes, project status updates, task status changes, timesheet workflow actions, and role assignments.

operations.description:
Retrieve a consolidated dashboard overview for the selected organization.

This endpoint provides a summary of key metrics and statistics for the currently selected organization. The data includes employee headcount, project status breakdown, timesheet submission rates, and recent activity logs. All information is strictly scoped to the selected organization context.

Security and Authorization: Only members who belong to the organization can access its dashboard. The operation validates that the user's employee record exists for the requested organization. No org:manage permission is required for basic overview data.

Data Context: All returned metrics are calculated based on the selected organization context. If the user belongs to multiple organizations, they will see data only for the organization they currently have selected in their session.

Related Operations:
- GET /projects — list and search projects in the organization
- GET /timesheets — retrieve timesheet records for the employee
- GET /activity-logs — retrieve detailed activity log records for the organization
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_tracker_organizations table to verify organization exists and user has employee membership. Count active employees from hrm_tracker_employees table. Aggregate project statistics from hrm_tracker_projects table including total, active, completed, and archived counts. Calculate timesheet summary from hrm_tracker_timesheets including submitted, pending, and overdue counts. Fetch recent activity logs from hrm_tracker_activity_logs table ordered by created_at descending with limit. Return aggregated summary statistics as IOverview type.

responseBody.description: Organization dashboard summary with key metrics

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated employee statistics and distribution metrics for a specific organization.

This operation calculates and returns key employee analytics including total employee count, active/deactivated breakdown, distribution by employment type (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern), and department-level statistics. It serves as a dashboard analytics endpoint for organizational oversight and workforce planning.

The operation enforces strict multi-tenancy: only users within the selected organization context can view its employee statistics. All data is automatically scoped to the organization identified by the organizationId path parameter. Deactivated employees are included in counts but excluded from active queries unless explicitly requested.

The request body allows optional filtering by department, employment type, and status to generate custom reports. When no filters are applied, the response provides a complete overview of the organization's employee composition.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_employees table with organization context.
Apply optional filters from request body: department_id, employment_type, status.
Calculate aggregate statistics: total count, active count, deactivated count.
Calculate employment type distribution using GROUP BY on employment_type.
Calculate department breakdown with employee counts per department.
Return paginated summary statistics rather than raw employee records.
Ensure organization_id from path matches organization context.

responseBody.description: Paginated aggregated employee statistics and distribution

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of audit records for employee role and permission changes.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive audit trail of all role assignment, change, and removal events within the organization. Each record captures who made the change, what the employee's role was before and after the change, when the change occurred, and from which IP address the action was initiated.

The audit trail is immutable and permanently recorded for compliance, internal review, and troubleshooting purposes. Records cannot be modified or deleted after creation, ensuring integrity of the historical record. This endpoint supports filtering by employee, actor (who made the change), date range, and action type to help investigators find specific events of interest.

Role change events include: role assigned (initial assignment to a new employee), role changed (replacement of one role with another), role removed (final termination of role assignment), and permissions updated (modification of permissions within the same role). All events are timestamped and linked to the employee whose status changed.

This audit feature supports organizational compliance requirements, internal governance, and detailed forensic investigation capabilities by providing a complete chronological history of role-based access changes.

The hrm_tracker_employee_role_changes table stores the complete history of employee role and permission changes. Each record captures the before and after state of the role assignment, the actor who made the change, the timestamp of the change, and the IP address from which the action was performed. This table is indexed by employee and actor for efficient querying and supports filtering by date range and action type.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_tracker_employee_role_changes table with pagination and filtering. Apply filters on hrm_tracker_employee_id, hrm_tracker_member_id, action_type, and changed_at date range. Join with related tables to include employee and actor details. Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of role change audit summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for role change audit records

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of system-generated activity logs for organization status history.

This operation provides access to the audit trail for all significant business events within the organization, including project lifecycle changes (creation, archival, completion, deletion), task status transitions, timesheet workflow actions (submission, approval, rejection), and role assignments. Activity logs are automatically generated by the system in response to business actions and cannot be manually created, edited, or deleted by users.

All log entries are scoped to the specified organization context, ensuring multi-tenancy isolation. Users must have org:manage permission to view activity logs.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_tracker_activity_logs table filtered by organization context. Join with hrm_tracker_members for actor information. Apply pagination and optional filters for action_type and target_entity_type. Return paginated summary results with activity log details optimized for list displays.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of activity log summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve an aggregated activity summary for a specific project.

This operation returns a summary of all activity logs related to a specific project, providing insights into project activity patterns over time. The summary includes aggregated data such as total activity count, activity breakdown by type, and timestamps of first and last activities.

**Authorization:**
- Members with project:view permission can view activity summaries for projects they are assigned to
- Deactivated employees retain visibility of their historical project activity summaries
- The operation respects organization data isolation - activity logs from other organizations are never exposed

**Activity Log Types:**
The summary includes all activity log types related to the project, including:
- Employee management actions (invited, deactivated, reactivated)
- Contract changes (created, edited)
- Project lifecycle events (created, archived, completed, deleted)
- Task status changes
- Timesheet workflow actions (submitted, approved, rejected)
- Role assignments and changes

**Data Persistence:**
Activity logs are preserved even when projects are archived or completed, ensuring complete historical visibility. Deactivated employees' activity contributions remain in the summary.
operations.name: summary
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_activity_logs table filtered by hrm_tracker_projects.id.
Join with hrm_tracker_employees and hrm_tracker_members to include actor information.
Group activity logs by date and action_type to compute summary statistics.
Return total count, activity breakdown by type, date range of activities, and most recent activity timestamp.
Apply organization-level data isolation to ensure only activities within the member's current organization context are returned.
Handle archived/completed projects by including all historical activity logs.
Return 404 if project does not exist or member lacks permission to view it.

responseBody.description: Project activity summary with aggregated statistics

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive dashboard information for a specific project.

This endpoint provides project members with a complete overview of the selected project, including project details, activity summaries, and relevant metrics. Only employees assigned to the project (either as regular members or project leads) can access this dashboard data.

The dashboard includes project name, description, color code, current status, budget information, schedule dates, and recent activity logs. This provides a centralized view for team members to understand project progress and context without navigating through multiple screens.

Related database schema: hrm_tracker_projects table contains project information including name, description, status, color, budget, start_date, end_date, and other project metadata.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_tracker_projects table by ID to retrieve project details. Join with hrm_tracker_project_members to verify the current employee is assigned to the project (either as member or project-lead). Include related hrm_tracker_timelogs and hrm_tracker_tasks for activity summary. Filter by project ID and employee assignment. Return project details with activity counts and recent status changes.

responseBody.description: Project dashboard data including details, activity summary, and metrics

operations.description:
Retrieve a hierarchical timeline view of all tasks within a specific project, including parent-child relationships.

This operation returns tasks organized in a tree structure where parent tasks include their directly assigned subtasks. This enables clients to render task timelines, Gantt charts, or nested task lists that respect the project's task hierarchy.

The timeline view preserves the project context and shows all tasks (both root tasks and subtasks) with their complete information including status, priority, assigned employee, and scheduling details. This operation is read-only and accessible to employees assigned to the project or users with project:manage permission.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_tracker_tasks table for all tasks where project_id matches the provided path parameter. For each root task (where parent_task_id is NULL), also query and include its directly assigned subtasks using the parent_task_id foreign key relationship. Return complete task objects with all fields including nested subtasks array. Apply project context validation to ensure employee has access to the project based on project visibility rules (assigned as member or project-lead). Do not apply soft-delete filtering since deleted_at check is handled at the service layer. Return hierarchical structure as root tasks with their subtasks attached.

responseBody.description: Hierarchical task timeline with parent-child relationships

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific project by ID.

This operation fetches comprehensive project details including name, description, color, current status, budget, and scheduled dates. Projects belong to organizations for multi-tenancy isolation and support status transitions between active, archived, and completed states.

Authorization requires project:manage permission for full access. Users with time:view_all permission can view project timelogs. The response includes all project metadata and relationships for detailed project information.
operations.name: statusChange
operations.specification:
Update hrm_tracker_projects table status field to the new value.
Validate user has project:manage permission.
Validate status transition is valid (active → archived/completed only).
Create activity log entry with action_type: 'project_archived' or 'project_completed'.
Ensure target project exists and is not soft-deleted.
Return updated project record with new status.

responseBody.description: Detailed project information

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated timelog analytics with filtering, grouping, and statistical summaries.

This operation provides comprehensive analytics capabilities for timelog data including time entries recorded by employees on projects and tasks. Users can apply filters by date range, employee, project, task, billable status, and organization to extract meaningful insights from their time tracking data. The system calculates totals for hours, billable hours, and non-billable hours across the filtered dataset.

**Security Considerations**
- Employees can only access their own timelog analytics
- Users with time:view_all permission can view timelog analytics across the entire organization
- The system enforces organization-level data isolation based on the employee's membership

**Data Relationships**
This operation leverages multiple related entities:
- hrm_tracker_timelogs contains the time entries with duration and billable flags
- hrm_tracker_employees links timelogs to specific employees
- hrm_tracker_projects provides project-level aggregation context
- hrm_tracker_tasks enables task-level time analysis
- hrm_tracker_organizations enforces multi-tenancy isolation

**Filtering and Search Capabilities**
The operation supports comprehensive filtering options:
- Date range filtering using start_date and end_date parameters
- Employee filtering to view specific employee's timelogs
- Project filtering to analyze time spent on particular projects
- Task filtering for detailed task-level time analysis
- Billable status filtering to separate billable from non-billable work

**Statistical Aggregations**
Calculated metrics include:
- Total hours across all matching timelogs
- Total billable hours for client billing tracking
- Total non-billable hours for internal work analysis
- Count of timelog entries for volume analysis

This operation is essential for time reporting, project budget tracking, and productivity analysis within the HRM tracker system.
operations.name: analytics
operations.specification:
Query hrm_tracker_timelogs table and aggregate data based on search filters.

1. **Employee Authorization**:
   - Regular employees: filter by current user's employee_id only
   - Users with time:view_all permission: access all employees' timelogs

2. **Filter Processing**:
   - Apply date range filters (date >= start_date AND date <= end_date)
   - Apply employee_id filter if provided (with permission check)
   - Apply project_id filter if provided
   - Apply task_id filter if provided
   - Apply billable filter if provided

3. **Aggregation Calculation**:
   - SUM(duration_in_minutes / 60.0) for total_hours
   - SUM(CASE WHEN billable THEN duration_in_minutes / 60.0 ELSE 0 END) for total_billable_hours
   - SUM(CASE WHEN NOT billable THEN duration_in_minutes / 60.0 ELSE 0 END) for total_non_billable_hours
   - COUNT(*) for total_timelogs_count

4. **Pagination**:
   - Apply offset and limit for result pagination
   - Return current page metadata

5. **Error Handling**:
   - Return 403 if employee lacks permission to view requested data
   - Return 400 for invalid date ranges or filter combinations

responseBody.description: Timelog analytics summary with aggregated statistics

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for timelog analytics

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated timesheet metrics and analytics for dashboard and reporting purposes.

This operation provides comprehensive analytics on employee time tracking across the organization. It aggregates timelogs from timesheets to deliver insights including total hours worked, time breakdowns by project and task, productivity trends, and employee contribution metrics.

The operation supports flexible filtering to analyze time data across different dimensions including date ranges, employees, projects, and tasks. Users can generate reports for specific time periods, individual employees, or organizational-wide summaries.

This analytics endpoint is designed for use by HR managers, project leads, and executives who need visibility into team productivity and time allocation without accessing individual timesheet details.

Security:
- Users with time:view_all permission can view all employees' timesheet metrics
- Regular employees can only view their own timesheet metrics
- Project leads can view metrics for all employees assigned to their projects

The operation aggregates data from the hrm_tracker_timelogs table joined through hrm_tracker_timesheets, calculating totals, averages, and breakdowns based on the applied filters. It supports complex multi-dimensional analysis while maintaining data isolation based on user permissions.

Apply filters for date range (week_start_date, week_end_date), employee ID, project ID, task ID.
Calculate total hours, averages, and breakdowns by project/task/employee.
Apply organization-level data isolation based on user permissions (time:view_all or project membership).
Return paginated summary statistics rather than individual timelog records.

Activity logs capture significant system actions including employee management (invited/deactivated/reactivated), contract changes, project lifecycle events, task status changes, timesheet workflow actions, and role assignments.

The endpoint supports comprehensive filtering and pagination. Response includes activity log summary information optimized for audit trail analysis and compliance reporting.

operations.description:
Retrieve organizational dashboard overview for members.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive dashboard view for members with report:view permissions, displaying key organizational statistics, pending invitations, recent activity logs, and current timelog summaries. The dashboard is designed for administrators and managers to quickly assess organizational health and identify pending actions.

The dashboard aggregates data from multiple sources including activity logs for recent system events, pending invitations for onboarding tracking, and timelog summaries for workforce activity. All data is filtered by the member's organization context to ensure proper multi-tenancy isolation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Aggregate dashboard data from hrm_tracker_activity_logs, hrm_tracker_pending_invitations, and hrm_tracker_timelogs tables. Calculate summary statistics for organization activity including pending invitation counts, recent activity log summaries, and current timelog aggregates. operations.description:
Retrieve the current active timer status for the authenticated employee.

This operation returns details about the employee's currently running timer, including the start timestamp, selected project, optional task, and description. If the employee has no active timer, the endpoint returns null.

The timer data updates in real-time, so any changes made to the active timer are immediately reflected in the response. This endpoint is designed to provide a live view of the employee's current time tracking session.

Access is limited to authenticated members with employee scope. The response only contains the authenticated employee's own active timer.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the hrm_tracker_timers table for the currently active timer associated with the authenticated employee. Use the employee ID from the authentication context to filter. Return the complete timer record if it exists, or null if no active timer is found.

responseBody.description: Current active timer details or null if no timer is running
